questions.prompt: One judge was fair, the other unjust.
questions.answer: Alter iūdex aequus erat, alter inīquus.

questions.prompt: Neither of the two leaders wished to consult the citizens.
questions.answer: Neuter dux incolās cōnsulere voluit.

questions.prompt: Each of the two brothers was cultivating his own field.
questions.answer: Uterque frāter suum agrum colēbat.

questions.prompt: To no one did the stern king grant peace.
questions.answer: Nūllī rēx rigidus pācem dedit.

questions.prompt: One tree bears figs, the other bears nothing.
questions.answer: Ūna arbor fīcōs fert, altera nihil.

questions.prompt: The shepherd feeds each of his two flocks with scanty grass.
questions.answer: Pāstor utrumque gregem exiguā herbā pāscit.

questions.prompt: Which of the two paths leads to the city?
questions.answer: Uter trāmes ad urbem dūcit?

questions.prompt: The other maiden gathered flowers with slender fingers.
questions.answer: Altera virgō exilibus digitīs flōrēs lēgit.

questions.prompt: Neither of the two consuls dared to relieve the besieged city.
questions.answer: Neuter cōnsul urbem obsessam levāre ausus est.

questions.prompt: The one or the other general will lead the wings of the army.
questions.answer: Alteruter dux ālās exercitūs dūcet.

questions.prompt: To each of the two soldiers the commander gave a reward.
questions.answer: Utrīque mīlitī imperātor praemium dedit.

questions.prompt: One wound was slight, the other deadly.
questions.answer: Alterum vulnus leve, alterum lētāle erat.

questions.prompt: Whichever of the two books you please, read it eagerly.
questions.answer: Utrumlibet librum avidē lege.

questions.prompt: No teacher praised either of the two poems.
questions.answer: Nūllus magister utrumque carmen laudāvit.

questions.prompt: One student sings, the other writes letters.
questions.answer: Alter discipulus concinit, alter litterās scrībit.

questions.prompt: The gift of the other friend revived my failing spirit.
questions.answer: Alterīus amīcī dōnum dēficientem animum meum recreāvit.

questions.prompt: One remedy is healthful, the other harmful.
questions.answer: Alterum remedium salūtāre, alterum noxium est.

questions.prompt: Each of the two old men was supporting his body with a staff.
questions.answer: Uterque senex corpus baculō sustentābat.

questions.prompt: Neither of the two rivers waters the dry fields.
questions.answer: Neuter amnis āridōs agrōs rigat.

questions.prompt: The vigor of one youth surpassed the strength of all the others.
questions.answer: Ūnīus iuvenis vigor cēterōrum vīrēs superāvit.

questions.prompt: One goddess blessed the fields, the other laid them waste.
questions.answer: Ūna dea agrōs beāvit, altera vāstāvit.

questions.prompt: Whichever of the two gods you please can save mortals.
questions.answer: Uterlibet deus hominēs servāre potest.

questions.prompt: Either of the two omens you please terrified the anxious king.
questions.answer: Utrumvīs ōmen rēgem anxium terruit.

questions.prompt: To neither of the two brothers did fortune grant a long life.
questions.answer: Neutrī frātrī fortūna longam vītam dedit.
